title: Ampleness on a finite disjoint union with integral point summands
statement: Let $I,J$ be finite sets, let $(Y_i)_{i\in I}$ and $(P_j)_{j\in J}$ be families of schemes [def-pc-scheme], and assume each $P_j$ is integral [def-pc-integral-scheme] with topological Krull dimension zero [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Form the disjoint union $Z=(\coprod_{i\in I}Y_i)\amalg(\coprod_{j\in J}P_j)$ [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family], with inclusions $a_i:Y_i\to Z$ and $b_j:P_j\to Z$. Let $\mathcal L$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_Z$-module [def-sc-invertible-module], with pullbacks as in [def-pc-module-pullback]. Each $P_j$ is isomorphic to the spectrum of a field [def-weil-field], and every invertible module on $P_j$ is ample. Moreover $\mathcal L$ is ample on $Z$ in the absolute sense [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module] if and only if $a_i^*\mathcal L$ is ample on $Y_i$ for every $i\in I$. Thus no condition on the $b_j^*\mathcal L$ is required. This includes empty index sets and empty $Y_i$.

source.place: Tag 01PS, definition-ample, applied to a finite disjoint union; the isolated-point summands in Varieties Tag 0B5Y, lemma-ampleness-in-terms-of-degrees-components.

proof.text: Fix $j\in J$ and write $P=P_j$. By [def-pc-integral-scheme], $P$ is nonempty and irreducible. By [lem-sc-scheme-sober], it has a unique generic point $\eta$. For any $x\in P$, the closure $\overline{\{x\}}$ is nonempty irreducible and closed. If it were properly contained in $P$, these two irreducible closed subsets would form a chain of length one, contradicting $\dim P=0$ in [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Hence every $x$ is a generic point of $P$ and uniqueness gives $x=\eta$. Thus $|P|=\{\eta\}$.

Choose an affine open neighbourhood $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $\eta$, which exists by the definition of a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Since $P$ has one point, $U=P$. Apply [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction] to the integral scheme $P$, its generic point $\eta$ and this nonempty affine open: $K=\mathcal O_{P,\eta}$ is a field. In the stalk description [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk], the only open neighbourhood of $\eta$ is $P$, so the germ map $\Gamma(P,\mathcal O_P)\to K$ is an isomorphism. As $\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}A,\mathcal O)=A$ by [def-weil-affine-spectrum], the affine presentation identifies $P$ with $\operatorname{Spec}K$.

Let $N$ be any invertible module on $P$. Local freeness of rank one [def-sc-invertible-module] gives a trivializing open neighbourhood of its unique point, necessarily all of $P$. The section corresponding to $1$ under $N\cong\mathcal O_P$ has nonzero value at $\eta$, so its nonvanishing open is the affine scheme $P$. Every open cover of a singleton has a one-member subcover. Hence $P$ is quasi-compact, and this section with exponent $1$ verifies [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]: $N$ is ample. By [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-invertible], each $b_j^*\mathcal L$ is invertible, so this applies to it.

proof.text: Suppose $\mathcal L$ is ample on $Z$. By [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family], each $a_i$ is an open immersion onto an open-and-closed subset, hence is a homeomorphism onto a closed subset. Therefore it is affine by [lem-trf-closed-embedding-affine]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-pullback-ample-invertible] to this affine morphism and the ample invertible module $\mathcal L$. It gives ampleness of $a_i^*\mathcal L$ for every $i$.

source.place: Tag 01PS (definition-ample), applied directly to the disjoint open cover; Varieties Tag 0B5Y (lemma-ampleness-in-terms-of-degrees-components), isolated point summands.

proof.text: Conversely assume every $a_i^*\mathcal L$ is ample. Each $Y_i$ is quasi-compact by [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module], and each $P_j$ is a singleton by Step 1. The disjoint open summands cover $Z$ by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]. For any open cover of $Z$, restrict it to each summand, choose a finite subcover there, and unite these finite choices. Finiteness of $I$ and $J$ makes this a finite subcover of $Z$. This proves quasi-compactness in [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme].

source.place: Tag 01PS (definition-ample), applied directly to the disjoint open cover; Varieties Tag 0B5Y (lemma-ampleness-in-terms-of-degrees-components), isolated point summands.

proof.text: Fix $z\in Z$ and identify its unique summand $W$ with the corresponding open-and-closed subscheme using [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]. Its restricted line module is ample, either by the assumption on the $Y_i$ or by Step 3. By [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module], choose $n\ge1$ and $s\in\Gamma(W,(\mathcal L|_W)^{\otimes n})$ with affine $W_s$ containing $z$. Pullback along an open inclusion is restriction by [def-pc-module-pullback]; iterating [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor](2) identifies this tensor power with $(\mathcal L^{\otimes n})|_W$. Regard $s$ as a section of the latter. On the disjoint two-open cover $Z=W\cup(Z\setminus W)$ glue $s$ to the zero section on $Z\setminus W$. This is the sheaf axiom for the module sheaf [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]: restrictions to the empty overlap agree, since a sheaf of abelian groups has just the zero section there. The resulting global section $\widetilde s$ of $\mathcal L^{\otimes n}$ has exactly the same germs as $s$ on $W$ and zero germs on the complement. Thus $Z_{\widetilde s}=W_s$, an affine open containing $z$. Together with Step 5 this proves ampleness of $\mathcal L$. No exponent has to be shared by different summands. If $I=J=\varnothing$, the cover argument makes $Z$ quasi-compact and the pointwise condition is vacuous; empty $Y_i$ cause no change.

Supporting finite disjoint-union ampleness and automatic ampleness on integral point summands (returned proof Steps 4-5).

split_report.summary: Q49 proves the point summands are singletons and spectra of fields, then proves automatic ampleness using a global frame. The forward implication uses affine pullback along clopen coprojections; the reverse implication proves quasi-compactness by finite subcovers and glues each local ample section to zero on the complementary open. All non-elementary facts already have nodes. No statement change and no new nodes. Searches cover the whole project, DAG and blueprint and use the required logged Mathlib search command.

The delivery adds 0 new nodes and leaves the statement unchanged; it matches the use in its citer lem-trf-fibre-degree-ample-criterion step 2. Step 1: integral plus dim 0 means the space is the single generic point, by sobriety (lem-sc-scheme-sober) and the length-1 chain argument (def-kun-topological-krull-dimension). Step 2: the affine chart is all of P; lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction makes O_{P,eta} a field, and with one neighbourhood the germ map is an isomorphism, so P = Spec K. Step 3: the trivialising neighbourhood is P, the frame section has X_s = P, so every invertible module on P is ample with n = 1. Step 4: the clopen open immersion is a homeomorphism onto a closed subset, so it is affine (lem-trf-closed-embedding-affine = Stacks 04DE, checked at morphisms.tex l.11338); lem-weil-pbc-pullback-ample-invertible then gives the forward direction. Step 5: finite subcovers summand by summand give quasi-compactness. Step 6: restriction to an open = pullback, iterated tensor compatibility (2), the local section glued with 0 on the complement, and Z_s~ = W_s affine. Source checked: Stacks 01PS (properties.tex l.4244) matches def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module. Edge cases checked: I=J=empty, I empty, Y_i empty, infinite J excluded, nonreduced Artinian points excluded by integrality.
